newsitem.title: CHINA: Hoechst in $16 mln China pigment venture.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst in $16 mln China pigment venture.

text.p: German pharmaceutical and chemical giant Hoechst Group has formed a new joint venture in northern China city of Tijian to produce pigments, a company official said on Thursday.

Hoechst (China) Investment Co and the Tianjin Dyestuff Factory No 8 jointly invested $16 million to set up the Hoechst Tianjin Pigments Co, with the German side investing 60 percent of the capital, she said.
The pigment venture was scheduled to be completed by early 1997 and would produce Azo pigments, which are widely used in paints, printing ink and plastic industries, she said.
The new plant would produce 3,000 tonnes of high-grade pigments a year and was expected to export 50 percent of the pigments to world markets, she said.
The Hoechst Group founded Hoechst (China) Investment Co in 1994 to coordinate and strengen its activites in China, she said.
Hoechst has so far invested a total of $450 million in 17 joint ventures in China, the official said.
